context: linear · foundations and ducts with the kerbs, poles after paving, energised circuit by circuit

brief.intro: New to this project type? Street lighting is a long chain of identical items: a foundation, a pole, a lantern, and a cable from pole to pole back to a feeder pillar and a control panel. None of it is difficult. Its timing is — street lighting is woven into the road works. The ducts and pole foundations must go in with the kerbs and before the footpath is paved, the poles are stood after the paving so they are not damaged, and the lanterns are lit only when the power supply to the feeder pillars exists. A road usually cannot be opened to traffic without its lighting, so the lighting sits near the end of the road programme with very little float.

scope.desc: Galvanised steel or aluminium poles, or high masts at junctions.

scope.name: Lanterns (luminaires)
scope.desc: LED lanterns with drivers and, often, a control node.

scope.name: Cables & pole cut-outs
scope.desc: Feeder cable looped pole to pole and the fused cut-out in each pole base.

scope.name: Feeder pillars & control panels
scope.desc: Supply and switching points, with photocell, timer or smart control.

scope.name: Earthing
scope.desc: Earth rods and bonding of every pole and pillar.

scope.name: Power supply connection
scope.desc: Supply from the distribution network to each feeder pillar.

scope.name: Testing & night-time measurement
scope.desc: Electrical tests and measurement of the lighting level on the road.

must_get_right: Install ducts and pole foundations with the kerb line, before footpath paving — finding a missing foundation after paving means breaking finished work.
Stand the poles after the paving and kerbs, and fit lanterns last; early poles get hit by plant.
The power supply to each feeder pillar comes from another contract or the authority; without it nothing can be tested or lit. Track it as a milestone.
Allow for the night-time lighting measurement and the municipality's inspection before the road opening date.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by road and lighting circuit (one feeder pillar), following the road-works sections.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar. Lux measurements are night activities; pole erection on live roads may be limited to off-peak hours.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Ducts and foundations follow the kerb line and precede footpath paving. Cable pulling follows ducts. Poles follow paving; lanterns and wiring follow poles. Energisation needs the feeder pillar and its power supply. Testing and the night measurement precede the road opening.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The road contractor releases each section for ducts and foundations in sequence; the power supply to the feeder pillars is available on the assumed date; pole positions are free of clashes with other utilities and driveways.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Works are in the footpath or median next to traffic and other trades. Pole positions are fixed by the lighting design and cannot be moved freely to avoid clashes.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: foundations or ducts missed before paving, clashes with other utilities at pole positions, late poles or lanterns, late power supply, and theft of cable. Contingency is held before the road-opening date.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by road and lighting circuit; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the foundation, cabling and erection crews — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
